Yoh HON. MARILYN SOCORRO H. CO Mayor, Municipality of Caramoan Province of Camarines Sur Dear Mayor Co: This has reference to your letter dated July 19, 2023 requesting legal opinion on Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) Elections and Imposed Suspensions. Specifically, the following points, which we quoted in toto, were raised for clarification: "(1) Is the Barangay and SK election considered a local election? I kindly ask for clarification on whether the Barangay and SK election is categorized as a local election within the context of our legal framework. Understanding the classification of this election is crucial in determining the appropriate application of pertinent laws and regulations. (2) Automatic lifting of preventive suspension under Sec. 62 (c) ofthe Local Govemment Code of 1991. Section 62 (c) of the Local Govemment Code of 1991 stipulates that no preventive suspension shall be imposed within 90 days prior to any election. Our computation indicates that the 90-day period preceding the scheduled 30th of October 2023 Barangay and SK Election commences on the ISt of August 2023. Consequently, we seek clarification as to whether any preventive suspension that was previously imposed will be automatically lifted on the ISt of August 2023. (3) Automatic lifting of suspension as a penalty on the election period. In accordance with the Omnibus Election Code, during the election period which will stan on 28th of August 2023, no preventive suspension or suspension as a penalty may be imposed without prior authority from the Commission on Elections (COMELEC). To ensure compliance with the law, we request a legal opinion on whether any suspension as a penalty that was previously imposed shall be automatically lifted on the 28th of August 2023. At the outset, we deem it proper to quote the following which are relevant to the issues you raised: Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

1) Section 62 of the Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), thus: . - (a) Within seven (7) days after the "SECTION 62. Notice of Hearing administrative complaint is filed, the Office of the President or the Sanggunian concerned, as the case may be, shall require the respondent to submit his verified answer within fifteen (15) days from receipt thereof, and commence the investigation of the case within ten (I O) days after receipt of such answer of the respondent. (b) When the respondent is an elective official of a province or highly urbanized city, such hearing and investigation shall be conducted in the place where he renders or holds office. For all other local elective officials, the venue shall be the place where the Sanggunian concerned is located. (c) However, no investigation shall be held within ninety (90) days immediately prior to any local election, and no preventive suspension shall be imposed within the said period. If preventive suspension has been imposed prior to the 90-dav period immediately precedinq local election. it shall be deemed automatically lifted upon the start of aforesaid period." (Emphasis Supplied) 2) Section 261 (x) of the Omnibus Election Code, thus: "Sec. 261. Prohibited Acts. - The following shall be guilty of an election offense: (x) Suspension of elective provincial, city, municipal or barangay officer. - The provisions of law to the contrary notwithstanding during the election period, any public official who suspends, without prior approval of the Commission, any elective provincial, city, municipal or barangay officer, unless said suspension will be for purposes of applying the "Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act" in relation to the suspension and removal of elective officials; in which case the provisions of this section shall be inapplicable. " Your first query was perhaps prompted by the use of the term "local election" in the highlighted Section 62 (c) of the LGC wherein 90 days prior to such local election, there shall be an automatic lifting of preventive suspension earlier imposed. As to what constitutes a local election, may we invite your attention to the Concurring Opinion of Justice Davide, Jr. in the case of Paras v. Comelecl , the salient part of which are as follows: The term "regular local election" must be confined to the regular election of elective local officials, as distinguished from the regular election of national officials. The elective national officials are the President, Vice-President, Senators and Congressmen. The elective local officials are Provincial 1 Danilo E. Paras, vs.Commission on Elections. G.R. No. 123169 November 4, 1996 Page 2 of 5

Governors, Vice-Governors of provinces, Mayors and Vice-Mayors of cities and municipalities, Members of the Sanggunians of provinces, cities and municipalities, punong barangays and members of the sangguniang barangays, and the elective regional officials of the Autonomous Region of Muslim Mindanao. [emphasis supplied] These are the only local elective officials deemed recognized by Section 2(2) of Article IX-C of the Constitution, which provides: Sec. 2. The Commission on Elections shall exercise the following powers and functions: (2) Exercise exclusive original jurisdiction over all contests relating to the elections, returns, and qualifications of all elective regional, provincial, and city officials, and appellate jurisdiction over all contests involving elective municipal officials decided by trial courts of general jurisdiction, or involving elective barangay officials decided by trial courts of limited jurisdiction. A regular election, whether national or local, can only refer to an election participated in by those who possess the right of suffrage, are not otherwise disqualified by law, and who are registered voters. One of the requirements for the exercise of suffrage under Section 1, Article V of the Constitution is that the person must be at least 18 years of age, and one requisite before he can vote is that he be a registered voter pursuant to the rules on registration prescribed in the Omnibus Election Code (Section 113- 118). Under the law, the SK includes the youth with ages ranging from 15 to 21 (Sec. 424, Local Government Code of 1991). Accordingly, they include many who are not qualified to vote in a regular election, viz., those from ages 15 to less than 18. In no manner then may SK elections be considered a regular election (whether national or local). (Emphasis Supplied) Taking into account the foregoing, barangay elections are considered local elections, while SK elections as sufficiently discussed above do not fall in either national or local elections. However, since the upcoming elections in October 2023 is denominated as "Synchronized Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections", the distinction is no longer relevant. As to your second and third queries, the following periods were mentioned: 1) Election period vis-å-vis the upcoming October 30, 2023 Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections, which per COMELEC Resolution No. 109052 was set from August 28, 2023 to November 29, 2023; and 2) 90-day period immediately preceding local election mentioned in Section 62 (c) of the LGC. 2 Entitled "REVISED CALENDAR OF ACTIVITIES AND PERIODS OF CERTAIN PROHIBITED ACTS IN CONNECTIONS WITH THE OCTOBER 30, 2023 SYNCHRONIZED BARANGAY AND SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN ELECTIONS (BSKE)". To better understand the effects of these periods, we made an illustration as follows: August 1, 2023 Election period October 30, 2023 (Election Day) August 28, 2023 90-day period per Sec. 62 (c), LGC November 29, 2023 Based on the foregoing, we clarify that: Starting August 1, 2023 up to October 29, 2023 [90-day period contemplated under Section 62 (c) of the LGC]—The sangguniang bayan, sangguniang panlungsod, sangguniang panlalawigan and the Office of the President can no longer impose preventive suspension upon local elective officials. If the sangguniang bayan, sangguniang panlungsod, sangguniang panlalawigan or the Office of the President had imposed preventive suspension upon local elective officials prior to Auqust 1.2023 and will last thereafter, such preventive suspension shall be deemed automatically lifted on August 1, 2023 [onset of the 90-day period under Section 62 (c) of the LGC]. Let it be noted that Section 62 (c) of the LGC categorically states that the lifting of the preventive suspension 90 days immediately preceding local election shall be "automatic" hence, without need of any further issuance for this purpose. Let it be noted further that Section 62 (c) of the LGC governs only those preventive suspensions imposed by the sangguniang bayan, sangguniang panlungsod, sangguniang panlalawigana and the Office of the President. It is inapplicable to the preventive suspension imposed by the Office of the Ombudsman and the Sandiganbayan, which are guided by different laws, rules and regulations as the Ombudsman Act and the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act. As regards suspension as a penalty, Section 62 (c) of the LGC only mentioned about the prohibition on the imposition of preventive suspension and does not include suspension as a penalty. Hence, suspension as a penalty may still be imposed by the sangguniang bayan, sangguniang panlungsod, sangguniang panlalawigan and the Office of the President notwithstanding the onset of the 90- day period on August 1, 2023. Page 4 of 5

As to the difference of suspension as a preventive measure and suspension as a penalty, the case of Quimbo vs. Gervaci03 is instructive, thus: "Preventive suspension is merely a preventive measure, a preliminary step in the administrative investigation. The purpose of the suspension is to prevent the accused from using his position and the powers and prerogative of his office to influence potential witnesses or tamper with records which may be vital in the prosecution of the case against him. If after such investigation, the charge is established and the person investigated is found guilty of acts warranting his suspension or removal, then he is suspended, removed or dismissed. This is the penalty." Starting August 28, 2023 to November 29, 2023 (election period), preventive suspension and suspension as a penalty imposed by the sangguniang bayan, sangguniang panlungsod, sangguniang panlalawigan, the Office of the President, and the Office of the Ombudsman cannot be implemented without prior approval from the COMELEC pursuant to Section 261 (x) of the Omnibus Election Code. Otherwise stated, preventive suspension and suspension as a penalty imposed by the sangguniang bayan, sangguniang panlungsod, sangguniang panlalawigan, the Office of the President, and the Office of the Ombudsman may still be implemented provided that they seek first the approval of COMELEC pursuant to Section 261 (x) of the Omnibus Election Code. Such COMELEC approval can be obtained by filing a request for exemption from the ban together with other supporting documents required. Let it be noted that Section 261 (x) did not mention about automatic lifting at the onset of election period of preventive suspension or suspension as a penalty earlier imposed. It only contemplates about the prohibition of implementation of preventive suspension or suspension as a penalty without COMELEC approval within said period. We hope to have sufficiently guided you on these issues. Thank you. Very truly yours, THORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AN TOR R.
